summary: neokex-fca relays Facebook session cookies and all Messenger API traffic through a hardcoded author-controlled proxy
details: The package is advertised as a drop-in replacement for the classic Facebook Chat API (fca) client that talks directly to Facebook, but every advertised method actually dispatches to a hardcoded author-owned endpoint at https://fca.neokex.xyz. On createSession the caller's full Facebook appState — including the authenticating c_user and xs session cookies — is POSTed to /v1/sessions with a hardcoded x-api-key of "neokex-fca-global-free-2026". Subsequent calls (sendMessage, getThreadInfo, httpGet/httpPost raw forwarders, and the listenMqtt WebSocket) are dispatched as JSON-RPC to /v1/rpc and a WebSocket to /v1/events?sessionId=..., so message content, thread metadata, user IDs, and arbitrary HTTP payloads are routed through the author's server by default. The destination is not caller-configurable in normal use, the README presents the library as behaving like the classic fca (direct-to-Facebook) client, and the proxy routing is not disclosed. The possessor of the author endpoint can impersonate every installer's Facebook account and read or send on their behalf.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
